messages:
alex_r: Seeing a spike of GPU OOMs on paged-attn workloads after yesterday's runtime roll. Perf traces attached, quick summary below.

josh: can you paste the trace snippet? which job? :eyes: 

alex_r: paste:
```
OOM at BlockMgr::alloc_block(size=1.2GB) -> failed to find contiguous slab
free_total=1.9GB, largest_free_contig=480MB, frag=68%
KV cache active entries=430k, avg_block_use=0.42
stack: allocator::alloc -> paged_attn::alloc_block -> kvcache::reserve
```

maria: FYI I rolled out the allocator slab split change (PR #2345) yesterday to reduce waste for many small allocations in the KV cache. It split large slabs into 256MB sub-slabs and changed free-list coalescing timing.

tina: that change was meant to help short-lived tensors, but it may increase the largest contiguous chunk size because coalescing is deferred.

josh: also noticed kernel selection fallback in the same timeframe. Runtime is picking the tiled-attn kernel only when workspace >= 600MB; otherwise it falls back to the slower 'fallback_gemm' which needs less workspace but is ~1.5x slower.

alex_r: here's a short repro run (reduced batch):
```
config: seq_len=2048, batch=8, kv_cache_slots=128M
observer: alloc_fail_count=12
kernel_fallbacks: 7 -> fallback_gemm
```

maria: hypothesis: slab split + deferred coalesce => fragmentation increases under sustained KV cache churn -> largest_contig < kernel workspace requirement -> kernel fallback + OOMs.

tina: agreed. Two immediate mitigation ideas: 1) reduce per-block requested workspace by preferring a smaller kernel variant for long sequences, or 2) reduce block size to lower compaction cost and increase reuse rate.

josh: quantitative numbers from profiling (30m window, p99):
- before PR: p99 alloc latency=12ms, token/s=14.2k
- after PR: p99 alloc latency=18ms, token/s=11.6k, OOMs=~1/hr

alex_r: cost of compaction also visible: compact() runs ~30x more frequently and consumes ~120ms/block when blocks > 8MB. Compaction pauses spike tail latency.

maria: can we try ephemeral background compaction during low-util windows (auto-throttle) instead of immediate coalesce on free? That would smooth latency.

tina: prototype CLI toggles I tested:
```
BLOCK_SIZE_BYTES=4194304  # 4MB (was 8MB)
COMPACT_DEPTH=2
COMPACT_THROTTLE_MS=50
DEFER_COALESCE=true
```

alex_r: ran an A/B on staging with BLOCK_SIZE=4MB, DEFER_COALESCE=true. Results over 1h:
- fragmentation down to 42%
- largest_contig up to 640MB on average
- kernel fallbacks reduced from 7->1
- token/s improved to 13.9k
- compaction ops increased but each op is cheaper (~60ms)

josh: nice. tradeoff: more total compaction work, but less OOMs and fewer slow kernels. latency tail improved.

maria: follow-up: batching heuristics also interact. Current batching window=20ms tries to maximize tokens but keeps many KV cache handles open, increasing churn. For long sequences we should favor smaller batching window or smarter coalescing of requests that share prefixes.

alex_r: proposal: add a policy so that when frag>50% OR kernel_fallback_rate>5% we temporarily switch to "compact-mode" where we reduce batch window to 10ms, lower allowed_inflight_per_gpu, and trigger background compaction at low CPU utilization.

tina: I'll open a small PR to expose the runtime flags and add metrics: allocator.fragmentation_ratio, largest_free_contig_bytes, kernel_fallback_rate, compaction_ms_per_op.

josh: also add a tracepoint on BlockMgr::alloc_block to capture chosen slab id and whether we later compacted that slab within 500ms. That will help confirm eviction/collision patterns.

maria: action items:
- revert slab-split rollout on prod for now (tina)
- run staged A/B with 4MB block size + defer coalesce (alex_r)
- add metrics and tracepoints (tina)
- add background compaction job guarded by low-util (josh)
- update kernel selector to prefer smaller-workspace kernel variant if frag>threshold (maria)

ci-bot: deploy job queued for rollback: deploy/allocator-revert -> status: queued :gear:

alex_r: temporary mitigation timeline: rollback in next deploy, then 48h A/B, then iterate. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

tina: saving logs to /var/logs/runtime/alloc-traces/1769990001.trace.gz and adding dashboard panel to infra -> eng-runtime -> allocator.

josh: I'll run the perf harness with seq_len sweep (512/1024/2048/4096) and post numbers tomorrow.

maria: capturing thread notes into the perf doc and will follow-up with a short RFC for long-term allocator redesign (slab defragmenter + async compaction).

alex_r: great. cc @product because this ties to Dedicated latency SLOs.

ops-bot: incident temp-alert created: ALLOC_FRAG_HIGH -> threshold=60% -> triggered on gpubox-12, gpubox-14

alex_r: end of thread — will paste the A/B summary next week.
